headline: Steady top-line growth undercut by a one-time tax hit
summary_short: Repligen's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose to $204M (+11.9% y/y, +5.1% q/q) with gross margin up to 53.9% from 51.0% a year ago, but net income fell to $5M (-66.3% y/y) as an effective tax rate spike to 64.6% — tied to the Q1 Polymem divestiture — offset the operating gains.
summary_long: Product revenue grew 11.9% y/y across all franchises (Filtration, Chromatography, Process Analytics, Proteins), broad-based geographically except a slight Europe dip. Gross margin expanded to 53.9% (from 51.0%) on favorable mix and overhead leverage. R&D rose on 908 Devices integration costs; SG&A rose on higher headcount; a $10.2M swing in contingent-consideration fair value also weighed on operating income. Net income fell 66.3% y/y to $5M as the effective tax rate jumped to 64.6% on the March Polymem divestiture (a $13.7M net loss) offsetting lower contingent-consideration tax benefits, plus higher FX and interest expense. Cash rose to $607M. On July 21, Repligen agreed to acquire BioLife for ~$1.5B, closing Q4 2026. No formal guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Revenue grew broadly and gross margin expanded on mix and overhead leverage, but net income fell sharply as a Polymem-divestiture-related tax charge pushed the effective rate to 64.6%.
Product revenue increased 11.9% y/y, growth widespread across all franchises; Asia Pacific/rest of world +36.1% and North America +11.2% over six months, while Europe grew a slower 7.2%.
Gross margin rose to 53.9% (from 51.0% y/y) on favorable product mix and improved leverage on indirect labor and overhead, even as cost of goods sold rose with higher sales volume.
Cost of goods sold rose 5.3% y/y, primarily driven by higher product sales, partially offset by improved leverage on indirect labor and overhead.

R&D (908 Devices integration) and SG&A (higher headcount) both rose, roughly offset by higher gross profit; a $10.2M unfavorable swing in contingent-consideration fair value also weighed on the total.

Not itself discussed by the company; this Yahoo-derived aggregate's y/y decline tracks roughly flat operating income plus higher other expense (FX) and higher interest expense below the operating line.

Investment income fell $1.1M on lower interest rates, interest expense rose, and other expense, net rose $4.2M on FX and financing items, all weighing on pretax income versus a year ago.
The effective tax rate jumped to 64.6% (from 18.4% y/y) primarily due to the Polymem divestiture, offset by lower contingent-consideration tax benefits, on top of lower pretax income.
